source: Crée un lobby inspiré de Fortnite avec une interface de menu en haut pour accéder facilement à la boutique et aux options d'achat. Conserve les skins d'origine des joueurs. Intègre deux modes de jeu fonctionnels : le Battle Royale et le Zéro construction (Zero Build), avec un départ en bus. Ajoute une boutique interne utilisant la monnaie virtuelle du jeu, les RFV-bucks, avec un Passe de combat à 800 RFV-bucks (obtenables dans le passe ou achetables), ainsi que quatre options d'achats distinctes pour obtenir des RFV-bucks directement avec des Robux.

image_prompt.text: An open lobby plaza where players gather before matches, sized for the full server without bottlenecking at the exits
A prominent lobby wall sized to host the global leaderboard
An out-of-play area off the lobby where players who are out wait and watch
The boarding point that carries everyone from the lobby into the match, read here as a bus standing ready to depart
two clearly signed lobby zones, one for each mode: Battle Royale and Zero Build
a large passenger bus parked in the lobby as the match departure vehicle

layout_placement.text: Detection regions that register round completion and placement in either mode
Markers that move everyone from the lobby onto the departing bus and into the match, and back to the lobby at round end
The global leaderboard data surface mounted on the lobby wall
A play boundary that contracts over the battle royale match, compressing survivors toward a shifting centre

notes: The lobby is the requested deliverable, so Party and Casual owns the shape; Shooter contributes the contracting boundary that Battle Royale implies. Close call on which genre is dominant.
P4 is unavoidable here: the match island is a separate map from the lobby. The prompt asks for two modes, which is arguably two stages, and the shape cannot say how many.
The top-of-screen menu, the shop, the RFV-bucks currency, the 800-cost battle pass and the four Robux purchase options are screen-space and monetization; none has a layout home.
Keeping players original skins is an avatar rule the layout cannot express.

open_questions.ask: A Fortnite-style lobby reads as bright stylized toon - is that the look you want, or something more grounded?
Should the lobby be a single plaza you can see across, or a larger hub with several buildings?
Do the two modes share one match map, or does each need its own?

coverage_missing.ask: Bright toon plaza, or a more realistic hangar-style lobby?
How large is the lobby - one plaza or a multi-building hub?
Do Battle Royale and Zero Build share a match map or need two?
Is the lobby purely a staging area, or do players do anything there besides shopping and queuing?

answers.ask: A Fortnite-style lobby reads as bright stylized toon - is that the look you want, or something more grounded?
answers.answer: Oui, je veux un style cartoon stylisé, lumineux et coloré, inspiré de Fortnite.

answers.ask: Should the lobby be a single plaza you can see across, or a larger hub with several buildings?
answers.answer: Un seul lobby compact sous forme de place principale, facilement lisible d'un seul regard, suffit.

answers.ask: Do the two modes share one match map, or does each need its own?
answers.answer: Les deux modes partagent une même carte de match ; la différence est simplement que le mode Zéro construction désactive la construction.
